BiblicalUsage: Amraphel was king of Shinar, and he appears only in the war of the kings in Genesis 14: he joined Chedorlaomer of Elam, Tidal king of nations, and Arioch of Ellasar against the five kings of the plain, and the four kings won the battle and carried off Lot, until Abram armed his trained servants, pursued them, and brought Lot back. Amraphel's name is never heard again after that chapter.
TheologicalSignificance: Amraphel is a king who won a battle and lost the war, and his whole story is two verses in a chapter about Abram. I believe that is the point: the kings of the earth make their alliances and take their spoil, and God still brings His man home.
